notes: Style choice: [CIP] says resets are asynchronous active low, assertion asynchronous and deassertion synchronised to the storage element's clock, chosen from a survey, team history and security analysis, with slightly more area and more care, and that the synchronous form needs a clock edge; [lowRISC] gives rst_n, the clock-qualified rst_domain_n and the always_ff form; [Rules] says not to use an asynchronous reset in a design and to test reset in the system-clock block. All found.

Release: AReset's three-flop synchroniser sets the flops and the output on the asynchronous reset and shifts a zero through on the clock; its contract (output high whenever input reset is active, high at least one clock before release, falls only on a rising clock edge, a cover of the release) is the property list in the document. The sentence that the reset must be active long enough to propagate is AReset's; the document tags the bullet [Chase], which has the one clock, two clocks, analogue lock and SDRAM figures. Both are in the bullet's sources, one tag short.

AxiReset: reset the registers and not the bus signals in an AXI-lite slave; the local reset may come from an input or a self-clearing bus register; retrofit with an AXI firewall rather than pulling the bus reset low; the local reset must reach the slave too, or a master can read results into the wrong address or hang. All found.

Gates: Verilator 5.052 was run with --lint-only -Wall over a small file with an asynchronous reset in one flop and a synchronous use of the same net in another; SYNCASYNCNET fired and the run failed. -Wall is -Wwarn-lint plus -Wwarn-style, and the style list on the Arguments page names SYNCASYNCNET; the Warnings page alone says only that it is a code-style warning off by default, so the document's [VLW] tag for -Wall membership leans on the Arguments page, which is not in this document's sources.
Chase's own story is that a three-cycle reset exposed a test that set constants during reset; the document does not use that and does not misstate it. Its testbench failure mode is tagged inference.
